title: Meta's Muse AI Agent Expands to Mexico and Opens Voice Video Access to All US Users

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The Muse assistant is now open to residents of Mexico, as the company expanded the availability of its conversational agent to the new market. Simultaneously, Meta broadened access to the app's real-time voice and video capabilities in the U.S., enabling all domestic users to hold live, lip-synced calls with AI agents that can be styled as people, animals, or other objects.

The software's video agents use a student model that reproduces the output of a teacher model in 2 passes per video chunk instead of 120, which supports portrait video at 25 frames per second. Meta stated that the integration of 4-bit quantization and dynamic batching allows one Nvidia GB200 to handle 12 concurrent video streams, with the agent beginning its reply about 870 milliseconds after a user stops speaking.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Adding 4-bit quantization, caching and dynamic batching lets a single Nvidia GB200 run 12 video streams at once.
selectedTweets.text:
Meta just opened live video calls with its Muse AI agent to every US user.

Callers see an animated avatar they can restyle as a person, animal or other character, and it reacts while listening.

Muse Realtime Voice emits speech tokens carrying words and delivery, and Muse Realtime Avatar turns the same stream into lip-synced video.

To run that live, Meta trained a student model to reproduce in 2 passes per video chunk what a teacher built in 120.

the system streams 448x768 portrait video at 25 frames per second and starts replying about 870ms after a user stops talking.

Adding 4-bit quantization, caching and dynamic batching lets a single Nvidia GB200 run 12 video streams at once.

In company-run tests of 2- to 3-minute calls, raters preferred the avatar to Runway Characters 78% to 22% and HeyGen LiveAvatar 88% to 12%.

At 12 streams per GB200, 1M simultaneous callers would need about 83K of them for video alone, so serving cost could cap the avatar’s reach.
